output_list.reason: The mintToken function allows the owner to mint additional tokens and assign them to any user account. This can lead to a devaluation of the token, as it increases the total supply and the token holder's balance without a corresponding increase in value. Attackers can exploit this to drain funds from the token contract.
The transferFrom function does not check for integer overflow, allowing users to transfer more tokens than available, causing a denial of service to other token holders.
The transfer function does not check for integer overflow, allowing users to transfer more tokens than available, causing a denial of service to other token holders.
The sell function does not check for integer overflow, allowing users to sell more tokens than available, causing a denial of service to the seller.
The mintToken function is public and not restricted, allowing anyone to mint additional tokens and assign them to any user account, potentially draining funds from the token contract.
